items.prompt: In the shown ordinary call, int&& named=10; category(named); selects which overload?

options.why: The expression consisting of the variable name is an lvalue here.

options.text: int& because named is an lvalue expression
options.why: Use std::move(named) to form the shown xvalue call.

options.text: No overload can bind any named variable
options.why: The int& overload can bind this modifiable lvalue.

options.text: const int& is required because literals are immutable
options.why: The named object here is not const.

items.explanation: Expression category and declared reference type are different; this ordinary C++20 call treats named as an lvalue.
